name: the-downside-up
description: The Downside Up: understand unfamiliar code in plain language. Explain functions beside the source, map the project's architecture and main flows, and explain what changed in files, with grounded, cached AI explanations.

enumDescriptions: Not configured. The preview offers model setup and local outlines; no AI requests.
A VS Code language model, such as GitHub Copilot, using your existing subscription. No API key needed; choose a model with “Downside Up: Choose Language Model”.
OpenAI Responses API with your own API key and separate API billing.
downsideUp.provider.description: Choose a model in the preview to enable AI explanations, comparisons and project summaries, or configure OpenAI below. Choosing a model sends no code and does not generate anything. Legacy mock settings require setup; placeholder generation is only available in extension development/test hosts. External requests require a trusted workspace and explicit per-repository and per-model consent.

downsideUp.preview.include.markdownDescription: Which items the preview lists besides functions and methods. All off gives a concise preview; turn items on for more detail. These descriptions are built locally and never call the AI.

types.description: Structs, enums, interfaces, traits, type aliases, implementations, and fields.

locals.description: Variables and constants declared inside functions.

functionComments.description: Source doc comments attached to functions and methods. Display only; comments remain available as AI context when hidden.

functionDetails.description: A one-line description of each function's parameters and results, and notes such as receivers or test roles.

downsideUp.explanations.showDetails.markdownDescription: Open the **More detail** part of AI explanations (where the function fits, edge cases, language notes, related code, and limitations) by default. It is part of every explanation, so changing this never regenerates anything.

downsideUp.explanations.formats.markdownDescription: Extra ways to show **What happens** in function explanations, as tabs next to the numbered steps. Enabled views are generated together with new explanations, which makes each request somewhat larger; for saved explanations, open the tab and choose **Generate**. Paired change comparisons include their Steps, Pseudocode, and Flowchart together in one request, either **Explain changes** or opted-in prefetch.

flowchart.description: A flowchart of the function's main path, decisions, and exits.

downsideUp.explanations.initialFormat.markdownDescription: Which view of **What happens** an explanation opens with, when it is enabled in `#downsideUp.explanations.formats#`.

downsideUp.hover.savedExplanations.markdownDescription: When hovering a call to a function, show the purpose from its saved AI explanation (in languages other than Rust and Go, calls are found with the editor's go-to-definition). Reads only the local cache and never generates. Works once the extension is active, for example after opening the preview.

enumDescriptions: One sentence per part of the project, plus how the parts connect. Component pages are filled in with Summarize.
Also a few sentences per component, with what it offers and what it uses, so component pages are filled in without a click. Makes the request that maps the project larger.
downsideUp.projectMap.detail.markdownDescription: How much the project map describes. The map is made with the repository overview, by the overview model, and drives what each folder preview shows: the project's parts, a group's members, or a component's internal parts. Changing this maps the project again with the next new explanation or **Refresh repository context**; nothing is sent until then.

downsideUp.languageModel.model.markdownDescription: The model that explains functions, when the provider is VS Code language models (for example `Claude Opus 4.5`). [Choose…](command:downsideUp.selectLanguageModel) from the models available to you. A new model asks once before code is shared.

downsideUp.languageModel.overviewModel.markdownDescription: The model for project-level work: the repository overview, folder summaries, and main flows. This is rarer than explaining functions, so a stronger model can pay off. [Choose…](command:downsideUp.selectOverviewModel) from the models available to you. Empty uses the model for explanations. A new model asks once before code is shared.

downsideUp.openai.model.description: OpenAI model for explanations, when the provider is openai (Responses API with your own API key). Changing the model requires renewed repository consent.

downsideUp.openai.overviewModel.markdownDescription: OpenAI model for project-level work, when the provider is openai: the repository overview, folder summaries, and main flows. Empty uses `#downsideUp.openai.model#`. A new model asks once before code is shared.

downsideUp.maxRequestSize.markdownDescription: The largest request, in KiB, for an explanation, an added pseudocode or flowchart view, a file or folder summary, or main flows. A request that would be larger is not sent, and you are told its size. Large functions with much related code need more; a smaller limit caps what each request costs. The model's own input limit also applies. Repository context uses #downsideUp.maxProjectContextRequestSize# instead.

downsideUp.maxProjectContextRequestSize.markdownDescription: The largest repository overview and project map request, in KiB, including previous context during reviews. If a review exceeds this budget, rebuilds from current bounded evidence in one request; inventory is shortened further if needed, with disclosed limitations. Raising this ceiling does not scan more files or start generation. The model's own input limit still applies. Can only be set in user settings.

downsideUp.maxConcurrentRequests.markdownDescription: How many AI requests may run at the same time. Your own requests always start before prefetches, and prefetching leaves one slot free for them (unless this is 1). Higher values make prefetching faster but can hit your provider's rate limits sooner; they do not change how many requests are made.

downsideUp.prefetch.enabled.markdownDescription: Generate AI explanations in the background for functions in the file shown in the preview, starting where you are reading and spreading outward. Also preloads the comparison when the preview first shows a Git diff, including paired Steps, Pseudocode, and Flowchart views. Uses your provider and its usage limits or billing without a click per function or diff. Runs only in trusted workspaces after code sharing was approved for the repository and model (and the overview model for normal files, if separate). The file preview offers an Approve sharing button while waiting; you can also explain a function or change first. Background work never asks for approval on its own or regenerates outdated comparisons after edits. Can only be set in user settings.

downsideUp.prefetch.window.markdownDescription: How many of the functions nearest to where you are reading are prefetched; the window moves as you move through the file. `0` prefetches every function in the file. Requires `#downsideUp.prefetch.enabled#`.

downsideUp.prefetch.dependencies.markdownDescription: For the function you are reading, how many of the functions and methods it calls in other files are prefetched (in languages other than Rust and Go, calls are found with the editor's go-to-definition), right after the function itself. Only the first calls in order of use are considered, and ones already explained count toward the number. `0` prefetches none. Requires `#downsideUp.prefetch.enabled#`.

downsideUp.exclusion.blockedFilePatterns.markdownDescription: [Choose file…](command:downsideUp.chooseBlockedFilePatternsFile) or [choose policy folder…](command:downsideUp.chooseExclusionFolder) and assign its files. [Check content exclusions…](command:downsideUp.checkContentExclusions) to inspect parsed rules or test a file locally. Saves to user settings only. Path to a text file of patterns for files that are never read into context or sent to a model provider, in any repository, in addition to `.gitignore` and `.copilotignore`. One gitignore-style pattern per line; blank lines and lines starting with `#` are skipped. Patterns are matched against paths inside the repository: a pattern without `/` matches at any depth (`*.vault` matches `config/app.vault`), a pattern with `/` is anchored at the repository root (`docs/private`), and a pattern matching a folder covers everything in it. `*` and `?` stay within one folder, `**` crosses folders. `~` is expanded. Read from user settings only. A missing or unreadable file adds nothing, so check the path. See the README for an example.

downsideUp.exclusion.restrictedRemotesFi.markdownDescription: [Choose file…](command:downsideUp.chooseRestrictedRemotesFile) or [choose policy folder…](command:downsideUp.chooseExclusionFolder) and assign its files. [Check content exclusions…](command:downsideUp.checkContentExclusions) to inspect parsed rules or test a file locally. Saves to user settings only. Path to a text file of Git remote URL prefixes, one per line (blank lines and lines starting with `#` are skipped). `*` matches any characters, and a trailing `*` is implied, so `ssh://git.example.com/` matches every repository on that server. A repository with any matching remote is not read or sent at all (explanations, file summaries, and **Refresh Repository Context** stop with the reason; the local preview still works) until it opts in with a `.copilotignore` file at its root or in a folder above it, a `.allowed-services` file at its Git root that contains the word `copilot`, or a listing in `#downsideUp.exclusion.allowedRepositoriesFile#`. `~` is expanded. Read from user settings only. A missing or unreadable file adds nothing. See the README for an example.

downsideUp.exclusion.allowedRepositories.markdownDescription: [Choose file…](command:downsideUp.chooseAllowedRepositoriesFile) or [choose policy folder…](command:downsideUp.chooseExclusionFolder) and assign its files. [Check content exclusions…](command:downsideUp.checkContentExclusions) to inspect parsed rules or test a file locally. Saves to user settings only. Path to a text file of repository paths, one per line (blank lines and lines starting with `#` are skipped), that may be sent even when `#downsideUp.exclusion.restrictedRemotesFile#` restricts their remote. A remote's path is its URL without the scheme, user, host and port, and `.git`, so `ssh://user@git.example.com:29418/team/app.git` has the path `team/app`. `*` matches within one path segment (`team/*` matches `team/app` but not `team/app/tools`), and the whole path must match. `~` is expanded. Read from user settings only. A missing or unreadable file adds nothing.

editor/title.when: (resourceScheme == file || (isInDiffEditor && resourceScheme == git)) && editorLangId != markdown && activeWebviewPanelId != 'theDownsideUp.explanation'

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Local code outlines and model setup are available without AI requests. External code sharing requires a trusted workspace, a configured model and explicit per-repository and per-model consent.
